One of my professors had generated AI images to go alone with her lecture notes to help students better understand what she was referring to. However, many students were left more confused from the image and didn't like that it had been taken from AI.

I think AI becoming a part of our education is inevitable, but the way educators are handling the issue isn't right. Teachers are still simply reprimanding students for AI use with a disciplinary notice. I think the right way to combat AI and adjust our curricula to it, it to inform students of the right and wrong way to use it so they can be clear of the guidelines and ultimately get the best from such a broad tool. As of right now AI is tipping more to the negative side because people don't know how to properly use it and are just getting short cuts.
